purpose: Independent practice of A9.1 — identifying and naming 2D shapes. Used as Lesson 1 consolidation artifact and as evidence for the diagnostic checklist.
student_learning_goal: I can identify and describe 2D shapes.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can identify and describe 2D shapes.
header.character_watermark: Sammy the Safari Sloth in the top-right corner of the header, smiling and holding binoculars. Small (~1.5in tall). References the shared 'Sammy the Safari Sloth' asset from blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Draw a line from each shape to its name.
parts.visual_layout: A two-column matching activity centred on the page. Left column shows 5 shape images in B&W line art (circle, triangle, square, rectangle, hexagon), each ~1.2in tall, stacked vertically. Right column shows 5 shape names ('circle', 'triangle', 'square', 'rectangle', 'hexagon') in scrambled order, also stacked vertically. A wide gap between columns invites the student to draw connecting lines.

image_placeholders.description: Five 2D shape thumbnails arranged in a vertical column for a Kindergarten matching activity. From top to bottom: circle, triangle (equilateral, point up), square, rectangle (wider than tall), hexagon. Each shape is a clean B&W outline ~1.2in tall, with no fill, suitable for printing. Generous spacing between shapes for easy line-drawing.
image_placeholders.placement: Left column of Part 1, vertically centred.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P1_SHAPES at left column of Part 1: the shape names listed in the right-column word bank (circle, triangle, square, rectangle, hexagon) match exactly the visual shapes drawn. Each keyword names a shape that the student must see and identify.

parts.answer_key: Each line connects each shape to its correct name: circle→circle, triangle→triangle, square→square, rectangle→rectangle, hexagon→hexagon.

parts.student_instructions: Look at each shape. Write R inside each ROUND shape. Write S inside each STRAIGHT-SIDED shape.
parts.visual_layout: A 2×4 grid of 8 shape thumbnails centred on the page, each cell ~1.4in square. Shapes shown: circle, triangle, oval, square, hexagon, rectangle, pentagon, semicircle. Each shape has a thin B&W outline with enough internal space for the child to write a single letter (R or S). Below the grid, two small legend boxes labelled 'R = round' (with a small circle icon) and 'S = straight-sided' (with a small triangle icon) remind the child of the code.

image_placeholders.description: An eight-cell shape grid in B&W line art arranged in 2 rows of 4. Top row left to right: circle, triangle, oval, square. Bottom row left to right: hexagon, rectangle, pentagon, semicircle. Each shape is centred in a square cell ~1.4in, no fill, ready to be coloured. Light borders separate cells.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P2_GRID at Part 2: student_instructions tell the child to colour ROUND or STRAIGHT-SIDED shapes. Visual shows shape categories that include round (circle, oval, semicircle) and straight-sided (triangle, square, hexagon, rectangle, pentagon).

parts.answer_key: ROUND shapes (write R): circle, oval, semicircle. STRAIGHT-SIDED shapes (write S): triangle, square, hexagon, rectangle, pentagon.

parts.part_title: Part 3: Find shapes in your classroom!
parts.student_instructions: Look around your classroom. Find 3 things that have a 2D shape. Draw each one. Write the shape name beside your drawing.
parts.visual_layout: Three rows of two-column workspaces stacked vertically. Each row has a left column for the drawing (a blank 2in × 1.5in box with a thin border) and a right column with a label line '____________ shape' for the child to write the name. To the right of all three rows is a small reference column with the 5 shape names stacked vertically (circle, triangle, square, rectangle, hexagon), so the child can copy the spelling.

image_placeholders.description: Three blank drawing boxes stacked vertically for a Kindergarten worksheet. Each box is ~2in wide × 1.5in tall, with a thin solid border, no fill or content. To the right of each box, a horizontal label line for writing the shape name. The full layout is suitable for a child to draw a classroom object then write its shape underneath.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P3_BOXES at Part 3: student_instructions ask the child to find 3 things in their classroom and draw them. The blank boxes provide drawing workspace; the keywords 'shape' and 'classroom' name what the activity is about.

parts.answer_key: Any 3 valid examples. Common: clock=circle, book=rectangle, door=rectangle, triangle ruler=triangle, window=square or rectangle, plate=circle. Accept any reasonable answer where shape name matches the object's primary 2D outline.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, draw 1 more shape from outside the classroom. Where do you see it?
teacher_notes: Lesson 1 consolidation artifact. Hand out at the end of the Action phase. Most children should complete Parts 1 and 2 independently. For Part 3, accept any valid match between drawing and shape name. Use Part 3 as evidence for the diagnostic checklist column 'Identifies shapes (independent)'. Children who can't complete Part 1 likely need a re-loop on shape names before moving to Lesson 2.
